memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go." — Josh 1:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the third time God calls Joshua to be strong and courageous, and now He adds the deepest reason. Notice the two enemies God names: fear and discouragement. Fear looks ahead at what might go wrong. Discouragement looks back at what has already gone wrong. Both can freeze us. God addresses both with one truth.

"Have I not commanded you?" God reminds Joshua that courage is not just a nice suggestion — it is a command. And that is a mercy, because God never commands what He will not enable. Behind every command of God stands the power of God.

Then comes the anchor of the whole chapter: "the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go." Not only in the easy places. Wherever. In the valley and on the mountain, in victory and in the waiting, God's presence is the constant.

This promise flows straight into the Gospel. Jesus took the name Immanuel, God with us, and His parting words to His followers were, "I am with you always" (Matt 28:20). For the believer, God's presence is not earned by our courage; it is the gift that makes courage possible.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which troubles you more today — fear of the future or discouragement over the past?
2. How does it change things to hear courage as God's command, backed by His power?
3. Where do you most need to remember that God is with you "wherever you go"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I bring You my fear and my discouragement. Remind me again that You are with me wherever I go, and let that steady my heart. Amen.
